approach: Add one path function, `paths::records_worktree(state_dir)` (`<state>/records-worktree`), beside `repo_state_dir`. Add `RecordSet::load_dir` and `RecordSet::load_current(git, treeish, worktree)` in athena-gate. `load_current` checks `worktree.is_dir()`. If the directory exists it reads `<worktree>/records/**` through `check_record_file`. Otherwise it calls `RecordSet::load(git, treeish)`. Add `Records::load_current(git, treeish, worktree)` in store.rs the same way. With a worktree it calls `Records::load_dir(worktree)`, which reads `records/` and `landings/` under the directory and goes through `from_parts`, so it assembles records exactly as `load` does. Without a worktree it calls `Records::load`. `Records::load_dir` is changed to take its `records/` half from `RecordSet::load_dir`, so the check-and-wrap code exists once. Its output is unchanged. Switch exactly three call sites to `load_current`, each passing `athena_data::paths::records_worktree(self.state.root())`: the `Records::load` and `RecordSet::load` calls in `Athena::status` (status.rs 988-989), and the `Records::load` call in `Athena::land_pr` (gh/landing.rs 846). The forecast is `class_forecasts(&records)` (status.rs 794, called at 1098) over the same `records` value, so it moves with the status load. Add tests in status.rs, gh/tests.rs, store.rs, gate records.rs and paths.rs. Use distinct job ids in the worktree and in-tree records/. Then add the follow-ups list (§14) to records-history.md and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: The worktree is probed first with `Path::is_dir()`. If it exists it is used, even when empty. records/ in the treeish is read only when the directory is absent.
decisions.reason: The request and the accepted reading say 'only when the worktree is absent'. An empty or partly written worktree must not silently fall back to frozen in-tree records.

rejected.option: Fall back when the worktree has no records/ or fails to parse
rejected.why: Hides a broken worktree behind stale records, which is what D111 moves away from.

decisions.choice: `paths::records_worktree(state_dir: &Path) -> PathBuf` takes the state directory (`StateDir::root()`) and returns `state_dir.join("records-worktree")`. `load_current` takes the worktree path as an argument.
decisions.reason: The path literal is defined once. The loaders in athena-core and athena-gate stay free of state-dir knowledge. Tests control the location through the `StateDir` they already pass to `Athena`, with no environment variables. `StateDir` is not in the deliverable list, so no wrapper is added there.

rejected.why: Tests would have to set `ATHENA_STATE_DIR`, which is global, or write into the real state directory. A test `Athena` uses `StateDir::new(temp)` and so never gets that path.
`state.rs` is not in the deliverables. Three call sites do not justify a new wrapper.

decisions.choice: Add `RecordSet::load_dir(dir)` in athena-gate and make `Records::load_dir` use it for the `records/` half. `read_files_under` stays for `landings/`.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-gate, not the reverse, so the gate crate needs its own filesystem loader. Sharing it means one copy of the check-and-wrap code. The existing test at status.rs 2820-2853 compares `load` with `load_dir` and keeps guarding the equivalence.

rejected.option: Build the worktree RecordSet from `git add` and ls-tree on a temporary index
rejected.why: Needs git state for a plain directory, and the worktree may be dirty.

decisions.choice: The forecast needs no separate loader. `class_forecasts(&records)` in `status()` reads the single value loaded by `Records::load_current`.
decisions.reason: Read at status.rs 794 and 1098. The test reads `StatusView.forecasts` through `Athena::status`.

rejected.option: A separate load for the forecast
rejected.why: It would give two sources inside one status call.

decisions.choice: The land_pr test uses the lookup's own outcome as evidence. A job found in the source gives 'has no verification', and an unknown job gives 'no job matches'. A no-origin repository and an erroring `Runner` keep the host out of it.
decisions.reason: `land_pr` first calls `reconcile`, which never fails (reconcile.rs 395-400) and returns early with no `origin` remote (404-407). Then it resolves the job and checks its verification before it touches the remote. So the test needs no host fake.

rejected.why: Pulls in remotes and CI state that are out of scope for a lookup test.

risks.risk: A worktree that exists but is empty or partly written makes status and land_pr see no jobs, with no fallback to records/. This is the chosen rule.
risks.mitigation: Production creates no worktree in this slice. The writer slice must create the directory only once it is complete. This is stated in the design doc follow-up text and covered by a unit test of the empty-directory case.

risks.risk: Until later slices move the other readers, a worktree could make status and land_pr disagree with commands that still read HEAD (drain `records()`, review, run).
risks.mitigation: The worktree does not exist in production yet, so no mix occurs. The design doc §14 lists the remaining readers as follow-ups, and the CHANGELOG entry says only these three moved.

risks.risk: Refactoring `Records::load_dir` to use `RecordSet::load_dir` might change the order or paths of files for snapshot users.
risks.mitigation: `RecordSet::load_dir` produces the same paths, relative to the directory with '/' separators and sorted by path. The existing tests that compare `load` with `load_dir` (status.rs ~2820-2853) and the snapshot.rs and gate_counts.rs tests guard it.

risks.risk: The forecast test needs a Request, a Job and a Score record that pass `check_record_file`. A malformed fixture lands in `records.invalid` and the test would pass or fail for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: The test builds each record as a typed `AnyRecord` and writes it at `canonical_path()` with `to_json()`. It asserts `view.invalid_records` is empty for each source, so a bad fixture fails the test.

risks.risk: status.rs is very large (132 KB), and an added test module could trip a size limit in code-health or lint checks.
risks.mitigation: The production change is two lines. Tests go inside the existing `#[cfg(test)]` modules, and the gh/tests.rs test goes in the existing test file, which the request names as the home of land_pr tests.

demonstrations.method: Three tests with 'records_worktree' in their names. In status.rs: a status test and a forecast test, each built on `crate::code_health::tests::set_up()`. In gh/tests.rs: a land_pr test on the same fixture. Each test commits one job into in-tree records/ through `athena.commit_records` and writes a different job's records under `paths::records_worktree(athena.state.root())`, using `record.canonical_path()` and `to_json()`. Status test: `Athena::status()`; the worktree job's id appears in `view.open` (queued request) and the in-tree id does not. Forecast test: the worktree job has a Request, a Job with `class_of_work` `class-wt` and a Score, the in-tree job has class `class-tree` with a Score, and `view.forecasts` lists only `class-wt`. Land_pr test: `athena.land_pr(<worktree id>, &ErrRunner, Poll{attempts:1,..}, &Quiet)` fails with 'has no verification', and `land_pr(<in-tree id>, ...)` fails with 'no job matches'.
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass: every reader sees the worktree's job ids and none of the in-tree ids while the worktree exists.
demonstrations.fails_without: If status, the forecast or land_pr still used `Records::load` on the treeish, the worktree job ids would be absent from `view.open`, `view.forecasts` would show `class-tree`, and `land_pr` of the worktree job would fail with 'no job matches'. All three assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `Athena::status` (status.rs 985) and `Athena::land_pr` (gh/landing.rs 832) are called as they are. Fixture: `crate::code_health::tests::set_up()` (exists, code_health.rs 1065) gives a temp git repo and a temp `StateDir`. The worktree is injected by writing files under `paths::records_worktree(athena.state.root())`, which plan step 1 adds. The `Runner` is a small test type whose `gh` always returns Err. It is never reached, because reconcile returns early with no origin and the lookup fails first. It holds none of the logic under test. `Runner` is the existing trait at gh/transport.rs 13.

demonstrations.method: The same tests, second half. After the worktree assertions, `std::fs::remove_dir_all(paths::records_worktree(athena.state.root()))`, then call the same entry points again. In-tree records/ job ids appear in `view.open`, the forecast shows `class-tree`, and land_pr resolves the in-tree job ('has no verification') and no longer finds the worktree job ('no job matches'). A store.rs unit test and a gate records.rs unit test cover the loaders directly: `Records::load_current` and `RecordSet::load_current` with a nonexistent worktree path equal `load(git, treeish)` for the same repo. With a worktree they equal `Records::load_dir` and `RecordSet::load_dir`, and an empty existing directory gives no records.
demonstrations.observes: Tests pass: with the directory absent the output matches the old `load` path, and an existing empty directory does not fall back.
